the first steps of the AGN feedback, when the AGN is not yet powerful enough to quench the star formation and the gas fraction is still relatively high.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in SBs, the AGN is still not able to efficiently quench the SBF, but the AGN is likely to be the dominant energy source in the host, heating the gas and dust, and possibly shaping the galaxy morphology.

, even in a sample of SBs, there are two distinct populations: one with a compact morphology and dominated by AGN emission, the other with a more irregular morphology and dominated by star formation.
, at z ~ 2, the AGN feedback has not yet kicked in for the majority of SBs.
the SBs are not yet the "dead" systems that will dominate the local population of red and dead galaxies.
